trust_decision.summary: The SAML Source ACS decides whether a signed assertion may log a user in. At the pinned commit ResponseProcessor.parse checks only the signature, the unsigned Response-level InResponseTo, Status and the Conditions time window. It does not check that the assertion was issued for this SP (Destination/Recipient/Audience) or bound to this SP's request (assertion-level InResponseTo). Replay is tracked only in IdP-initiated mode, keyed on the unsigned Response ID.

landing_point.why: ResponseProcessor.parse is the single validation pipeline for SAML Source responses. 'Assertion confusion' leads straight to its _verify_* calls at lines 99-101 and to _verify_request_id at 201.

fix_sites.module_kind: same file. _verify_request_id: Response-ID replay list removed, InResponseTo accepted from the Response or from bearer SubjectConfirmationData (fix.diff:34085-34113)

same file. New methods inserted before _verify_status: _get_bearer_confirmation_data, _verify_destination, _verify_subject_confirmation/_check_subject_confirmation (Recipient, NotOnOrAfter, InResponseTo), _verify_not_seen_before (atomic cache.add keyed by source and sha256(assertion ID)) (fix.diff:34115-34202)
module constants. CACHE_SEEN_REQUEST_ID replaced with a per-assertion cache key and timeout plus the bearer method constant (fix.diff:34064-34069)
HTTP view wrapper. The except clause is widened to SAMLException/SuspiciousOperation so the new exceptions give a 400 (fix.diff:35138-35149). Error mapping only, not security-critical.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All security-relevant changes sit in authentik/sources/saml/processors/response.py. The views.py:159 change only maps errors. No second implementation of SAML response consumption exists: ResponseProcessor is built only at authentik/sources/saml/views.py:156 outside tests, and the provider side builds responses but does not consume them.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: With allow_idp_initiated (authentik/sources/saml/models.py:113-119, documented in its help text as 'no validation of the request ID is done'), a solver can argue the IdP-initiated path is opted-in and unbound by design, so it needs no Recipient/Destination binding and no assertion-ID replay check. Response-level Destination/InResponseTo look like they are 'already checked', although only the assertion is signed by default (models.py:205-206).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Behaviour that must keep working: IdP-initiated logins with no InResponseTo when allow_idp_initiated is on; Responses with no Destination attribute; assertions with several SubjectConfirmations where any one valid bearer confirmation is enough; InResponseTo present only on SubjectConfirmationData; case-insensitive ACS URL compare; encrypted assertions. An over-broad fix (Destination always required, every confirmation must match, or IdP-initiated rejected) breaks these. The fix's updated tests patch build_full_url to keep existing IdP fixtures passing (fix.diff:34020-35112 range, test_response.py hunks).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Conditions/AudienceRestriction is never compared with this Source's entity ID (get_issuer), so 'issued for another SP' is still decidable only via the optional Recipient/Destination
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The published fix chose Recipient/Destination as the binding. Conditions is already 'validated' for its time window, and Audience is optional in practice with many IdPs.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; the source's entity ID comes from authentik/sources/saml/models.py:252-256

O8_uncovered_routes.route: When a bearer confirmation has no Recipient and the Response has no Destination, the published checks pass by omission (absent means accept), so binding rests entirely on the IdP including the attributes
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Spec interoperability: SAML marks Destination as optional for unsigned Responses, and rejecting its absence could break IdPs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An AudienceRestriction check that only inspects the first Audience element or the first AudienceRestriction
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _verify_conditions already walks Conditions with .find (single-element) idioms. Multiple AudienceRestriction elements are AND-ed by spec, which a maintainer could easily get wrong.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The binding checks read get_assertion() while property mappings/user_info use a different assertion lookup (e.g. root.find of the first Assertion), giving a signed-vs-consumed identity differential
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_assertion already has a fallback to an unsigned lookup, and user_info passes both root and assertion (response.py:272-276, 337-342). A mapping helper could plausibly re-query root.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The session request ID is never consumed after a successful ACS. A legacy or alternate ACS path (e.g. a stage-embedded source) could re-use it without the assertion-ID cache.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Nothing pops SESSION_KEY_REQUEST_ID after use (only set at request.py:44, read at response.py:212-218).
